kf: Potency ladder (UK): **mild** (hydrocortisone 1%), **moderate** (clobetasone butyrate 0.05%), **potent** (betamethasone valerate 0.1%, mometasone 0.1%), **very potent** (clobetasol propionate 0.05%).
Match potency to **site and severity**: mild on face and folds, potent on body, very potent on palms and soles for short courses.
Dose with **fingertip units**: 1 FTU ≈ 0.5 g covers two adult palms (about 2% body surface).
Usually once or twice daily; for eczema, treat flares fully then step down or use **weekend (proactive) therapy**.
Side effects come from misuse: atrophy, striae, perioral dermatitis, steroid rosacea, **topical steroid withdrawal**; under-treatment from **steroid phobia** is commoner.
myths: **"Steroid creams thin the skin, so use as little as possible"**: correct potency for a short course is safe; under-treatment prolongs flares.
patho_lead: Corticosteroids **switch off inflammatory genes** in skin cells.

mech.t: Steroids cross the cell membrane and bind the glucocorticoid receptor.
The complex suppresses NF-κB and AP-1 (inflammatory genes) and induces anti-inflammatory proteins.
Anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive, vasoconstrictive and antiproliferative effects.
Thin skin (eyelids, genitals, folds) absorbs far more than palms and soles.
mech.cap: Relative absorption varies widely by body site.

mech.t: Prolonged potent use thins epidermis and dermal collagen.
mech.cap: Steroid atrophy: thinned epidermis and dermis.

comp: Atrophy, striae, telangiectasia, acne, rosacea, perioral dermatitis, infection masking (tinea incognito), HPA suppression (rare, large amounts).
prog: Safe and effective when the right potency is used for the right time.
